page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. It provides 48 dedicated physical cores powered by the Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is configured at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARM AES instructions, does not include GPUs, and provides no local bundled storage, necessitating external network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark testing demonstrates the advantages of its high core count and single-threaded core execution. In multithreaded processing, the instance recorded a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 87,022.37 and achieved an elevated Geekbench software compilation score of 39,151.0. Conversely, single-core metrics show limitations, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,110.0 and bzip3 single-threaded decompression registering 8.87 GB/sec, placing it in lower performance tiers for serial compute. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached large-block read bandwidth of 181.23 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 78.56 GB/sec. Static web serving reached 34.9 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value processing achieved 61.65 million Redis SET operations per second.

The absence of SMT guarantees predictable core isolation, eliminating cross-thread contention on shared execution units. This architecture delivers consistent operational efficiency for scale-out parallel computing without hypervisor resource oversubscription. Given its balanced resource distribution, solid compilation metrics, and multi-core throughput, the t2a-standard-48 is best matched for parallelized software build pipelines, containerized microservices, web application serving tiers, and distributed continuous integration environments optimized for the Arm ecosystem.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-48 is an Arm-based general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 physical cores clocked at 3.0 GHz with single-threaded execution. Equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, it maintains a standard 4.0 GB per core memory profile. The instance includes hardware AES encryption support, contains no discrete GPUs, and provisions no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disks for filesystem hosting. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits strong multi-core scalability, achieving 87,022.37 on stress-ng multi-core and 39,151.0 on Clang software compilation benchmarks, offset by modest single-threaded performance. Memory throughput remains balanced, supporting 61.65 million Redis SET operations per second and 34.9 GB/sec of static web traffic. The absence of hyperthreading eliminates thread contention, making the instance well structured for distributed CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration, microservices clusters, and scale-out web serving workloads built for the ARMv8 architecture.
